Project Title: Towards Self-Improving Language Models via Adaptive Reinforcement Learning with Limited Data Accessibility on Local Devices  
Authors/Affiliations: K. Ravikumar (Ph.D student, School of Computer Science and Engineering), Dipanwita Pal (Assistant Professor) & Siva Shankar (Professor). The project is a part of the BCSE306L course at King's College London under Dr. Peter Minka for Fall 2term 2023, with funding from Huawei and support through Turing Award-winning AI researcher Ivo Daiberberg.
---  
ABSTRACT: With the exponential growth of language models (LMs) like GPT and BERT in various tasks such as content generation or text summarization, their deployment on local systems without internet access remains a challenge due to limited data availability for further training post-deployment. Our project introduces an adaptive methodology that enables LMs trained offline with minimal supervision—relying primarily on the model's predictions and confidence levels rather than extensive human feedback or large labeled datasets typically required by modern models like GPT3/4. This approach is applicable to language-centric tasks in healthcare, education, etc., where data can be scarce but critical for sensitive applications such as patient diagnostics. Our methodology comprises two phases: adaptive and self-critical training strategies that enhance the model's understanding of its capabilities by reflecting on past decisions while simultaneously learning from feedback received during task execution to improve future responses, thus reducing error propagation risks associated with deploying untrained models. Initial experimental results show promising improvements in performance metrics when compared against traditional fine-tuning methods like self-training and model distillation approaches using just a few human labels for guidance. Our findings underscore the significance of adaptive learning techniques to extend LMs' usefulness beyond cloud environments, especially where access or reliability issues exist concerning internet connectivity while maintaining reasonable resource requirements on local systems—with potential implications that span across diverse sectors needing automated language processing solutions in low-connectivity settings.
---  
Keywords: Language Models (LM), Self-Improvement, Local System Deployment, Adaptive Learning Strategies, Limited Data Accessibility, Error Propagation Reduction
